polls.question: Can binding autonomous weapons rules be achieved by 2028?

cluster_stories.title: UN talks pledge to draft ‘killer robot’ rules by 2028 after Russian pushback
cluster_stories.summary: UN talks on regulating weapons with little or no human oversight ended on Saturday with a pledge ‌for further discussions to develop new rules within two years, an outcome weakened by Russia’s opposition and disappointing human rights groups. Proponents had called for legally binding rules within a short time frame to regulate weapons systems that can identify and engage targets with varying degrees of autonomy, sometimes called “killer robots”. cluster_stories.headline: UN Pledges Autonomous Weapons Rules by 2028 Despite Russian Opposition

cluster_stories.title: Countries open path towards ‘killer robots’ pact
cluster_stories.summary: After five days of talks at the United Nations, which dragged on into overtime, states agreed on building some form of pact over the next two years.
cluster_stories.headline: Nations Agree to Draft Autonomous Weapons Pact by 2028

cluster_stories.title: Chinese national Li Ming charged in fraud case in Singapore linked to Megaspeed and Alice Huang: Report
cluster_stories.summary: Li Ming, a Chinese national, is facing fraud charges in Singapore regarding alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. He was involved with Megaspeed, a company linked to Alice Huang, the former romantic partner of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang. Li is accused of misleading an American supplier by misrepresenting the intended destination of purchased servers. Following an investigation, Megaspeed was placed on a no sell list by Nvidia.
cluster_stories.headline: Chinese National Charged in Singapore Nvidia Chip Fraud Case
